definition: Careful not to reveal much about your thoughts, feelings, or plans.
example: The researchers expressed guarded optimism about the early results of their new battery design.
nuance: Reserved describes a quiet temperament, while guarded suggests deliberately holding back in a particular situation, often out of caution.
prompt: On her first day, a new student is asked by classmates about the school she left.
options: Her guarded replies revealed little beyond the name of the town she had left.
Feeling guarded, she poured out every detail of her old friendships and quarrels.
She was guarded highly by classmates who admired her from the moment she arrived.
A hall monitor stood by her desk, so her answers were guarded.
reasons: Sharing only a bare fact and holding the rest back is exactly this kind of caution.
Telling everything freely is the opposite of holding back.
This confuses the word with "regarded," which means thought of or esteemed.
The word describes a cautious manner, not answers watched over by a person on duty.

practice.prompt: A reporter asks a shop owner whether sales will improve next year.
options: The owner was guarded, cheerfully promising that profits would triple by spring.
The owner felt guarded because a tall iron fence surrounded the store.
The owner was guarded, yelling at the reporter to leave and never come back.
The owner was guarded, saying only that it was too early to make predictions.
reasons: A bold, confident promise reveals plenty and shows no caution.
A fence offers physical protection, but the word here means holding back what you say.
Open hostility goes too far; the word suggests quiet caution, not angry outbursts.
Avoiding a firm answer and giving away little shows careful restraint.
